subject.title: [Feature]: Expose before_tool_call/after_tool_call in internal hooks system

question: Should managed internal HOOK.md hooks become a synchronous tool-call policy surface, or should blocking and parameter rewriting remain limited to typed plugin hooks?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested fix changes the trusted-code boundary around shell, file, and plugin tool execution and could create a second policy API with different semantics from plugin hooks.

options.title: Design managed tool-call hooks
options.body: Add a typed managed before/after tool-call contract with explicit fail-open/fail-closed, timeout, block, rewrite, audit, docs, and test coverage before implementation.

options.title: Keep policy plugin-only
options.body: Document that HOOK.md hooks are operator automation only, keep enforcement in typed plugin hooks, and surface unsupported tool lifecycle event names clearly in hooks info/loading.

options.title: Expose observe-only hooks
options.body: Allow after-tool or telemetry-style HOOK.md observation while leaving pre-execution blocking and parameter rewriting in the plugin hook API.

recommendation.title: Design managed tool-call hooks
recommendation.body: Add a typed managed before/after tool-call contract with explicit fail-open/fail-closed, timeout, block, rewrite, audit, docs, and test coverage before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the internal-hook history and explicit discussion signal keeping this as the canonical tracker.
